inspection_summary: Inspected all 659 normalized lines. The mathematical core develops a reusable chain from Jacobi last multipliers and Lie symmetries to alternative Lagrangians, Noether symmetry selection, symmetry-preserving quantization, and canonical linear reductions for two modified xp Hamiltonians. The source's RH relevance is an explicitly negative spectral diagnosis: the analyzed symmetry-preserving quantizations still have continuum spectra. Formula damage is localized and flagged rather than silently reconstructed, especially the displayed Schrödinger equation at lines 351-355, the coefficient at line 333, and the broken repeated heading fragment at lines 508-510.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic metadata plus an abstract-level statement of the Hilbert-Polya motivation, modified xp Hamiltonians, Lie-Noether quantization method, and continuum-versus-discrete spectrum question.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the desired spectral realization, three proposed classical-system constraints, the failure of bare xp, two bounded-trajectory modifications, and the paper's symmetry/Lagrangian program.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Jacobi last multiplier, Lie symmetries, Lagrangians
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds the general mechanism relating first integrals, transformation laws, divergence equations, symmetry determinants, Jacobi multipliers, Lagrangian Hessians, gauge freedom, and families of Lagrangians.

sections_inspected.label: 3. The case H = x(p + ell_p^2/p)
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives a linearizable second-order equation, contrasts Lagrangians and their Noether algebras, constructs symmetry-preserving quantum equations, reduces them canonically, and diagnoses continuum spectrum; page apparatus and a damaged next-heading fragment are non-mathematical or extraction-defective.

sections_inspected.label: 4. The cosh-weighted Hamiltonian case
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Shows a second eight-symmetry linearizable model, its free-particle representation, and the contrast between a multiplier-derived five-Noether-symmetry Lagrangian and the Hamiltonian-derived three-symmetry Lagrangian.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Final Remarks and acknowledgments
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Synthesizes linearizability, nonuniqueness of Lagrangians, symmetry selection, and the persistence of continuum spectra; closes with acknowledgment material.

sections_inspected.label: References
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliography only; inspected for boundary completeness and not selected as semantic units.

accepted_units.title: From Hilbert-Polya constraints to modified xp Hamiltonians
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the desired self-adjoint spectral realization from classical design constraints and explains why bounded-trajectory modifications of xp are introduced before Lie-Noether quantization.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit includes the criteria, failure of bare xp, two proposed modifications, and the stated analysis route; the abstract and quoted motivation are not needed to interpret it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed Hamiltonians are text-layer legible, but superscript/subscript typography should be retained; no numerical evaluation is involved.

accepted_units.title: Jacobi last multiplier from complementary first integrals
accepted_units.why_material: Gives the determinant identity defining a multiplier and explains its dependence on a chosen independent set of first integrals, a reusable bridge between differential equations and invariant densities.
accepted_units.context_note: The displayed determinant at lines 158-175 is layout-heavy but its role is explicitly stated in the surrounding prose.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires determinant layout and distinction between the vector field A, first integrals omega_i, and multiplier M; scan consultation is advisable before reusing the exact matrix typography.

accepted_units.title: Multiplier covariance, divergence equation, and ratios as first integrals
accepted_units.why_material: Collects three structural facts: Jacobian covariance under a change of variables, equivalence with a linear divergence equation, and conversion between pairs of multipliers and first integrals.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit continues from the definition of a JLM but restates each property sufficiently for local interpretation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Jacobian fractions and the total derivative in the logarithmic equation must preserve numerator/denominator order.

accepted_units.title: Lie symmetries determine a Jacobi multiplier by an inverse determinant
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces prior knowledge of first integrals with n-1 infinitesimal symmetries and constructs the multiplier as the inverse determinant of the dynamics and symmetry coefficients.
accepted_units.context_note: Overlap with the preceding unit retains the prose bridge from first integrals to Lie's symmetry formulation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The determinant matrix is visually structured; its exact rows should be checked against the page image before formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: A Jacobi multiplier is the velocity Hessian of a Lagrangian
accepted_units.why_material: Connects a second-order equation to variational form: a multiplier integrates twice to a Lagrangian, while the integration freedom is organized by a gauge function and one constrained residual term.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Euler-Lagrange relation, the double-integration construction, and the gauge decomposition so the bridge is not reduced to a bare formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on distinguishing partial derivatives in q-dot and on nested integral layout; prose makes the mechanism recoverable, but exact formula typography should be verified for reuse.

accepted_units.title: Pairs of Lie symmetries generate families of multipliers and Lagrangians
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how multiple symmetries of one second-order equation produce multiple determinant multipliers and hence multiple Lagrangian representations of the same dynamics.
accepted_units.context_note: The determinant specializes the general symmetry construction to the prolonged second-order vector field.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prolonged coefficients dG/dt - q-dot dV/dt and determinant row ordering are formula-layout dependent and should be scan-verified before exact transcription.

accepted_units.title: An abelian intransitive symmetry subalgebra linearizes the Sierra equation
accepted_units.why_material: Uses the eight-dimensional sl(3,R) point-symmetry algebra to select a canonical two-dimensional subalgebra and transform the nonlinear Lagrangian equation to the free-particle equation.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Hamiltonian, induced second-order equation, symmetry algebra, canonical subalgebra target, and resulting point transformation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The transformation coefficient printed as '12' at line 333 is damaged fraction typography. The linearization claim and variable dependence are accepted from prose, but that coefficient is not reconstructed and requires scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A multiplier-derived Lagrangian carries five Noether symmetries
accepted_units.why_material: Instantiates the general multiplier pipeline: the selected linearizing symmetry pair yields a Lagrangian with the maximal five Noether symmetries used to constrain quantization.
accepted_units.context_note: Stops before the damaged displayed Schrödinger equation while retaining the explicit transition to symmetry-preserving quantization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact L78 polynomial/exponential formula has dense layout and should be scan-checked; the symmetry list and selection claim are readable.

accepted_units.title: The five-symmetry quantization has continuum spectrum
accepted_units.why_material: Records the decisive negative result for the first quantization and checks that the resulting equation inherits five Lie symmetries corresponding to the classical Noether generators.
accepted_units.context_note: The antecedent is the Schrödinger equation displayed at lines 351-355, whose extraction is damaged; this unit accepts only the prose continuum-spectrum conclusion and readable symmetry-inheritance structure, not a reconstructed equation.

accepted_units.title: A different Lagrangian reduces its symmetry-preserving quantum equation to the same linear classical normal form
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that another multiplier/Lagrangian choice yields a different parabolic equation whose change of variables removes spatial derivatives, and relates that reduction to a member of the classical linear family.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the alternative Lagrangian, five Noether symmetries, parabolic equation, canonical reduction, general solution, and correspondence with the transformed classical equation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Lagrangian fraction and symmetry correction terms require mathematical typography; the transformations and canonical equations are readable in the normalized text.

accepted_units.title: The Hamiltonian-derived Lagrangian is not recovered from the indicated symmetry-pair multiplier at the limiting parameter
accepted_units.why_material: Distinguishes the original Sierra Lagrangian from a parameterized multiplier-derived Lagrangian and exposes a singular limit: their formulas coincide at A=0 exactly where the determinant multiplier from the selected pair ceases to exist.
accepted_units.context_note: The surrounding family of equations explains what the arbitrary parameter changes and why equality of Lagrangian expressions does not preserve derivational lineage.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Square-root placement in the displayed Lagrangians and multiplier is layout-dependent; the singular determinant statement is explicit prose and is not inferred from OCR algebra.

accepted_units.title: Three-Noether-symmetry quantization reduces to an ordinary equation and still has continuum spectrum
accepted_units.why_material: Derives a second symmetry-preserving parabolic equation, reduces it by an invariant variable to an ordinary linear equation, matches that form to the classical linearized family, and supplies the second continuum-spectrum route summarized later.
accepted_units.context_note: The spectrum conclusion is stated in the final remarks at lines 588-589; this unit contains the construction that conclusion refers to.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mixed derivatives and exponential solution factors are readable but exact operator normalization should retain the displayed coefficients.

accepted_units.title: The cosh-weighted model is linearizable, but its natural and multiplier-derived Lagrangians preserve different symmetry counts
accepted_units.why_material: Transfers the same symmetry analysis to a second proposed Hamiltonian and contrasts a five-Noether-symmetry multiplier-derived Lagrangian with the three-symmetry Hamiltonian-derived Lagrangian, while noting a singular linearizing map.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the clean Hamiltonian definition at lines 512-516, induced equation, free-particle reduction, two Lagrangians, symmetry-count contrast, and stated decision not to repeat the analogous lengthy analysis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The duplicate heading fragment at lines 508-510 and several square-root/nested-trigonometric formulas are damaged or layout-sensitive. No missing formula is reconstructed; exact transformation (50) and Lagrangians (51)-(52) require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Symmetry choice explains representation changes but does not remove the continuum-spectrum obstruction
accepted_units.why_material: The author explicitly synthesizes the chain: eight-dimensional linearizability, many Lagrangians, a unique maximal-Noether class up to representation, distinct three-symmetry Hamiltonian Lagrangians, and continuum spectra for both studied quantizations.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a source-authored conclusion, not independent evidence that the broader spectral program fails or that no other symmetry choice can work.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant; generator labels and parameter A must remain linked to the constructions in section 3.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The symmetry-multiplier-variational pipeline
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: First integrals or Lie symmetries can construct Jacobi multipliers; multipliers both transform as densities and integrate to Lagrangians; multiple symmetry choices therefore expose multiple variational representations of one second-order dynamics.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a structural pipeline stated for the differential-equation setting in the source, not a claim that every resulting Lagrangian has the same Noether algebra or quantum interpretation.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Classical linearizability reappears in reduced quantum equations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The large point-symmetry algebra linearizes the classical equation, and alternative symmetry-preserving parabolic equations reduce under invariant-variable changes to members of the same simple linear family.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The correspondence is established for the displayed models and changes of variables; it does not by itself determine spectral boundary conditions or self-adjointness.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Variational representation controls the preserved quantum symmetry interface
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Different Lagrangians for related classical dynamics admit different Noether subalgebras, and preserving those different subalgebras selects different quantum equations even when their canonical reductions remain simple.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source compares particular multiplier-derived and Hamiltonian-derived Lagrangians; it does not exhaust all Lagrangians or quantization prescriptions.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The cosh model transfers the symmetry-count contrast
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The second modified xp Hamiltonian repeats the pattern that a linearizable equation admits a richer multiplier-derived Lagrangian than the Hamiltonian's natural Lagrangian, while also introducing a singular linearizing transformation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source explicitly declines the lengthy analogue of the full first-case quantization analysis, so no unreported spectral conclusion for this second model is inferred.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Continuum spectrum is the source's bounded negative RH result
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: For the two symmetry-preserving quantum equations actually analyzed in the first model, symmetry-guided construction does not furnish the desired discrete Riemann-zero spectrum because both are reported to have continuum spectra.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This excludes neither other symmetry choices nor other Hamiltonians, and the source does not claim an RH proof or refutation.

within_source_saturation: Saturated for semantic segmentation: every usable mathematical line is represented as a unit or supporting context; additional selections would repeat the introduction/final summary, isolate routine displayed algebra from an already represented mechanism, or rely on formula-damaged text requiring scan verification.
